item.title: Ex-Border Patrol commander Bovino was under investigation when he retired
item.description: CBP informed Gregory Bovino in an email on March 2 that the agency was "conducting an official Inquiry into allegations of misconduct reported to CBP." He initiated retirement 16 days later.

item.title: Ford recalls nearly 149,000 Mustang vehicles over potential power issue
item.description: A potential wiring issue could lead to vehicles losing power or disruption of other functions, such as windshield wipers and headlights.

item.title: Tankers attacked as Trump mulls new strikes in "little war" with Iran
item.description: Two oil tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as President Trump threatened further strikes on Iran, while downplaying the "relatively little" six-month war.

item.title: H.R. McMaster reacts to Army Secretary Dan Driscoll's wartime resignation
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll handed his resignation to President Trump after months of disagreements with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Retired Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster reacts.

item.title: Gold's price is down by over 21%. Where will it head this September?
item.description: Gold enters September well below its recent price peak, and several factors could determine where prices go next.

item.title: MapQuest hits No. 1 on App Store after refusing to rename Lake Ontario
item.description: MapQuest topped ChatGPT as Apple's most-downloaded free app after the digital mapping company said it would keep "historical, familiar" lake names.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial jury deadlocked, but judge tells them to keep deliberating
item.description: The jury in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial can't come to a unanimous decision, they told a judge after entering their fourth day of deliberations Tuesday in Massachusetts.

item.title: Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary pits age against ideology
item.description: Younger centrist Seth Moulton and older progressive Ed Markey are fighting for the Senate nomination in the Massachusetts Democratic primary. CBS News congressional reporter Taurean Small has more.

item.title: Victim in Times Square stabbing, shooting identified as Bank of America employee
item.description: Erin Piacenti was identified as one of the two people stabbed by a woman Monday afternoon in Times Square before police shot and killed the suspect.

item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard could make landfall in Texas or Louisiana
item.description: Texas and Louisiana are bracing for Tropical Storm Edouard, which could make landfall today. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: IRS audit revenue plunged following mass layoffs, watchdog finds
item.description: IRS audits collected $3.5 billion less in fiscal 2025 as the agency shed thousands of auditors and other agency staffers.

item.title: Oil prices rise again as U.S. renews Iran strikes
item.description: Energy and gas prices are up again after the U.S. resumed strikes on Iran. CBS News' Kelly O'Grady has more on the economic outlook.

item.title: U.S. Treasury official on economic goals at G20 summit
item.description: Chris Pilkerton, assistant secretary for investment security at the U.S. Treasury Department, is at the G20 summit in Asheville, North Carolina, and joins CBS News with more on what to expect.

item.title: Trump to meet with U.S. oil executives amid Pentagon infighting
item.description: President Trump will meet with U.S. oil executives over the price of oil. This comes after Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation following months of friction with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. CBS News' Olivia Rinaldi has more.

item.title: John Ternus is Apple's new CEO, replacing Tim Cook
item.description: John Ternus is stepping up and into the shoes of former Apple CEO Tim Cook. CBS News' Jo Ling Kent reports, plus Puck AI correspondent Ian Krietzberg shares his thoughts on the Apple turnover and the Hugging Face AI breach.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Grand Canyon flood deaths lead to questions about alert system
item.description: Dr. John Giusti and Brent Rosenkranz died in major flash floods in the Grand Canyon. A third man, Timothy Allen Smith, is still missing.

item.title: Spain's leader says Russia and Israel fueled immigration "disinformation"
item.description: Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says "networks linked both to Russia and to Israel" helped spread rumors about immigration "to attack Europe and divide it."

item.title: Watch: Lindsay Clancy jurors say they're deadlocked, judge sends them back for deliberations
item.description: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial said Tuesday they were deadlocked on their fourth day of deliberations. The judge told them to return to deliberations.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial jurors tell judge they are deadlocked
item.description: Jurors in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy are saying they are deadlocked on Day 4 of deliberations. Plymouth Superior Court Judge William Sullivan has asked them to keep deliberating. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul and Caroline Polisi have more.

item.title: Lionel Richie hospitalized after weekend show
item.description: While performing in St. Louis on Saturday night, Lionel Richie appeared at one point to lean on a piano for support, according to video from the show.

item.title: U.K. man accused of drugging, abusing wife with other men goes on trial
item.description: The case has drawn parallels to that of Gisèle Pelicot, who publicly testified against her ex-husband in a 2024 mass rape trial.

item.title: Whistleblower warns Postal Service's mail ballot portal is "rushed," "untested"
item.description: The whistleblower, described by lawyers as a federal official, disclosed information about the Postal Service's new mail-voting procedures to Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut.

item.title: 3 friends went hiking in the Grand Canyon. 2 died, 1 is still missing.
item.description: At least two people were killed after flash floods swept through parts of Grand Canyon National Park over the weekend.

item.title: See which jobs could grow fastest — and slowest — over the next decade
item.description: New federal labor figures forecast the fastest-growing U.S. job sectors over the next decade.

item.title: Grand Canyon rescue teams hold out hope as search intensifies for missing hiker
item.description: At least two people were killed in flash flooding in the Grand Canyon over the weekend and one person is still missing, officials said, as search efforts intensify Tuesday. Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: U.S.-Venezuela oil deal will rely on North American Blue Energy Partners
item.description: The Trump administration's plan to take a stake in tens of billions of barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves will hinge on a private company called North American Blue Energy Partners, the White House announced Monday.

item.title: Trump inks deal with 9 pharmaceutical companies to lower drug costs
item.description: The White House said the agreements will reduce costs to treat Parkinson's disease, macular degeneration, glaucoma, liver disease and other illnesses.

item.title: At least 1 killed, 5 injured in shooting at rave in Switzerland
item.description: Local police said early Sunday a manhunt was underway and the motives were still unclear.

item.title: Man with sinus infection symptoms diagnosed with heart condition
item.description: Marc Gaudisosi thought his symptoms were caused by a sinus infection. Then an urgent care told him to go to the hospital.
